articleTitle: Space-qualified Additive Manufacturing and its Application to Active Antenna Harmonic Filters
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE MTT-S International Microwave Filter Workshop (IMFW)
abstract: The objectives of this paper are to introduce a new manufacturing technique for space applications, and to present a harmonic filter for active antennas in Ka-band, both developed by SWISSto12. The new manufacturing technique is based on metal 3D printing followed by plating for insertion loss enhancement. The end-to-end manufacturing technique (including the plating) has been qualified and has already flight heritage. The conception of the harmonic filter is used to explain the main steps of the manufacturing process.

articleTitle: X-Band 3D-Printed Metal-Insert Twist-Component for Bandpass Filter Applications
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE MTT-S International Microwave Filter Workshop (IMFW)
abstract: This work presents the development of an X-band twisted metal-insert bandpass filter as a monolithic 3D-printed structure. The component serves as a compact solution for the incorporation of a fourth-order bandpass filter response while simultaneously rotating the polarization by 90 degrees as a twist-component. The structure is fabricated using low-cost stereolithography 3D-printing and metallized using a simple copper electroplating method. The measured results exhibit an unloaded Q-factor of approximately 2600 and have an insertion loss better then 0.44 dB throughout the passband, ultimately demonstrating a unique use of the metal-insert filter technique and providing a novel presentation on integrated monolithic structures.

articleTitle: Design Guidelines for Microwave Filters in Gap Waveguide Technology
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE MTT-S International Microwave Filter Workshop (IMFW)
abstract: In this paper, the effects of each physical parameter of a gap waveguide structure on the key factors for the design and realization of gap waveguide bandpass filters (BPFs) are discussed and a set of design guidelines is presented. Based on the proposed design guidelines, a third-order differential bandpass filter with intrinsic common-mode suppression is designed, fabricated, and measured for demonstration. Practical considerations regarding the EM power leak from the gap waveguide cavities are also highlighted.

articleTitle: Triangular Combline Filters Conceived for Additive Manufacturing
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE MTT-S International Microwave Filter Workshop (IMFW)
abstract: This paper presents, for the first time, a new type of combline filter. This filter, which has been conceived for Additive Manufacturing, uses triangular irises and cavities in order to enable a geometry that is vertically 3D printable. To validate the new concept, a filter with fractional bandwidth of 1.8% at 11 GHz has been designed, manufactured, and tested. The work in the article was performed by SWISSto12 with the support of MAXAR Technologies.

articleTitle: Microfluidic-Based Ultra-Wide Tuning Technique for TM010 Mode Dielectric Resonators and Filters
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE MTT-S International Microwave Filter Workshop (IMFW)
abstract: This paper introduces a new technique of designing widely frequency tunable TM010 mode dielectric-loaded waveguide resonators and filters. The proposed tuning method is based on using liquid metals to tune the resonant frequency by altering the liquid level inside the resonator hollow-channel. A single-pole bandpass filter is designed, fabricated, and measured for proof-of-concept purposes. The realized filter demonstrated wide frequency tuning from 2.33 GHz to 0.67 GHz maintaining low insertion loss < 1 dB allover the tuning window. The presented results exhibit the great potential of the proposed technique in high-performance widely-tunable next-generation RF systems.

articleTitle: Fully Inline and Symmetric Dual-Mode Dual-Band Bandpass Filters for Millimetre-wave Applications
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE MTT-S International Microwave Filter Workshop (IMFW)
abstract: This work presents the design of inline dual-mode dual-band bandpass filters with flexible center-frequency allocation for application at millimetre-wave frequencies. In this design, resonators are configured for the TE101 and TM120 modes without perturbations or tuning means and allow for the control of two separate fourth-order passbands within the filter while remaining fully inline and symmetric. A presentation on the basic filter design and several examples with different center-frequency locations are presented within the W-band. A prototype with center frequencies at approximately 86.3 GHz and 100 GHz is fabricated and tested. The measurements demonstrate exceptional unloaded Q-factor results for the W-band, ultimately, validating the design approach.

articleTitle: Very High Q-Factor Bandpass Filter Using Additive Manufacturing
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE MTT-S International Microwave Filter Workshop (IMFW)
abstract: A spherical bandpass filter is presented. The main feature of the proposed filter is the use of the spherical mode TE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">101</inf>, which presents a higher unloaded Q-factor than the fundamental mode and its proximate higher order modes. As a result, in this work, the mode TE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">101</inf> has been exploited in the design of a 2-pole filter with a central frequency at 10 GHz and fractional bandwidth 1.2%. The fabrication has been carried out using the selective laser melting technology in order to exploit the flexibility of additive manufacturing. In particular, two monolithic prototypes have been manufactured. Good agreement between measurements and simulations have been observed, with almost identical results between the two manufactured prototypes, thus proving the repeatability of the process. No tuning screws have been used.

articleTitle: Dielectric TM Dual-Mode Filters with Y-shape
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE MTT-S International Microwave Filter Workshop (IMFW)
abstract: In this paper, the realization of Y-shaped dielectric dual-mode resonator filters is discussed. All resonators are composed by uniform cylindrical rods which can be soldered on different metallic cores. This enables different resonator geometries to be realized easily. The dual-mode resonators are designed to operate in the TM mode. A second order Y-shaped dual-mode filter with one real frequency axis transmission zero (TZ) as well as two different fourth order filters are designed, manufactured and measured within this paper. Depending on the geometry, the fourth order filters either reveal a complex TZ pair or even a pair of real frequency axis TZs.

articleTitle: Overview of Base Station Requirements for RF and Microwave Filters
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE MTT-S International Microwave Filter Workshop (IMFW)
abstract: As is commonly acknowledged, the frequency spectrum is the most valuable resource in wireless communication, and filter is the key component for its efficient utilization. Filter solutions vary greatly in different base transceiver station (BTS) system. To be more specific, metal cavity filters are dominant in 4G macro BTSs, while dielectric filters and miniaturized metal cavity filters are widely used in 5G base stations. Indoor small base station mainly uses acoustic filters or dielectric mono-block filters, and point-to-point microwave backhaul system mainly uses waveguide filters. The evolutionary trend of filter technology is different for the different BTSs which are introduced in this paper. The special process in filter manufacture, namely, tuning is also discussed.

articleTitle: Ka-band Coaxial Horn Filtenna for Enhanced Electromagnetic Compatibility on Spacecraft
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE MTT-S International Microwave Filter Workshop (IMFW)
abstract: Coexistence of wireless data links and radio sensing instruments onboard scientific satellites renews challenges concerning electromagnetic compatibility. Integration of filtering functions into the downlink antenna offers a space-effective way to improve isolation by suppressing out-of-band emissions. The present manuscript describes a filtenna design based on insertion of radial stubs into a coaxial horn and provides simulated results validating the principle.

articleTitle: Dual-Band Filter Composed of Dielectric and Waveguide Resonators with In-Band Transmission Zeros
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE MTT-S International Microwave Filter Workshop (IMFW)
abstract: This paper presents the design of a hybrid narrowband dual-band bandpass filter with in-band transmission zeros (TZs) in the Ku-band, whose passbands are realized by different types of resonators. The upper passband is realized by waveguide resonators, while the lower one is implemented by TE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">01δ</inf> mode dielectric resonators (DRs). The filter synthesis process is based on using frequency transformation. To validate the mixed resonator design, the proposed filter is manufactured and the measurement results are compared with the simulation. The passbands of the manufactured filter are designed for a bandwidth of 40 MHz and center frequencies of 13.47 GHz and 14.05 GHz, respectively.

articleTitle: A New Resonant Coupling Structure for Inline Waveguide Filters with Transmission Zeros
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE MTT-S International Microwave Filter Workshop (IMFW)
abstract: In this work a novel resonant coupling structure in rectangular waveguide is introduced. The proposed structure allows the introduction of transmission zeros in the response of inline filters. The main advantage with respect to the resonant couplings usually adopted (i.e., resonant posts) is that the new structure allows the placing of transmission zeros very close to the passband. Moreover, it does not require any extra space as instead does the stopband singlet recently introduced for the same purpose. An equivalent circuit of the novel coupling structure is proposed, suitable for the use in the synthesis of filters with frequency-dependent couplings. Dimensioning charts are then introduced, to make it easy the initial assignment of the physical dimensions of the structure so that the extracted equivalent parameters have the assigned values. Finally, an example of use of the novel coupling structure in a 6-2 waveguide filter in Ka band is presented.

articleTitle: Design of Cavity Resonators Applying Shape Deformation Techniques
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE MTT-S International Microwave Filter Workshop (IMFW)
abstract: In this paper, the shape deformation technique for geometry optimization of microwave structures is introduced. The proposed scheme offers high flexibility in shaping the geometry of a device and is specifically aimed at the design of microwave structures, such as cavity resonators for additive manufacturing. The deformation scheme is coupled to an eigen-mode solver of an electromagnetic field simulator based on the 3D finite-element method (FEM). This gives greater flexibility in the design of a resonant cavity thanks to the introduction of additional degrees of freedom and allows for better control on the electrical parameters of resonators, including the quality factor or higher order mode separation. To show the advantages of shape deformation in resonator design, an example of the design process is shown.

articleTitle: Ceramic-loaded Barrel-shaped Ku-band filter for High-power Satellite Applications
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE MTT-S International Microwave Filter Workshop (IMFW)
abstract: In this paper the first experimental results of a very compact Ku-band bandpass filter for high-power applications based on dielectric-loaded combline resonators are shown in the framework of an ESA ARTES AT project. Architectures and materials have been chosen in order to improve the performance in terms of power-handling and multipactor up to 150 W continuous wave of the input RF power. Barrel-shaped metal cavities are combined with high-permittivity ceramic materials in order to minimize the volume occupation maintaining high unloaded Q-factor values (>4500). A 6<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">th</sup> order elliptic filter has been manufactured and results concerning environmental and high-power tests are presented here.

articleTitle: Multilayered Balanced Wideband Bandpass Filter With High Filtering Selectivity
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE MTT-S International Microwave Filter Workshop (IMFW)
abstract: A type of multilayered balanced wideband bandpass filter (BPF) with high filtering selectivity is presented. It is composed of two back-to-back cascaded microstrip-to-microstrip vertical transitions using slotline stepped-impedance resonators (SIRs). Under differential-mode excitation, a sharp-rejection fifth-order wideband filtering transfer function with two paired close-to-passband transmission zeros can be attained in the proposed balanced BPF. Moreover, high common-mode suppression levels within the differential-mode passband range are achieved. For experimental-demonstration purposes, a microstrip prototype of the devised balanced wideband BPF architecture is developed and tested. It exhibits a measured differential-mode fifth-order high-selectivity wideband filtering response with center frequency of 4.015 GHz, 3-dB fractional bandwidth of 38.06%, and minimum in-band power-insertion-loss level of 0.947 dB. The common-mode suppression levels are above 20 dB from 2.075 to 5.588 GHz.

articleTitle: 3D Printed Microwave Components for Frequencies above 100 GHz
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE MTT-S International Microwave Filter Workshop (IMFW)
abstract: In this work, 3D printing technology is investigated as a potential manufacturing technique for waveguide components for frequencies above 100 GHz. Two components fabricated by micro laser sintering (MLS) process are outlined and discussed here: a D-band (110-170 GHz) diplexer and H-band (220-330 GHz) filter. Both devices are comprised of rectangular waveguide cavities and made of two split blocks of stainless-steel. The results are promising and they demonstrate that good dimensional accuracy has been achieved by the MLS printer. However, both devices exhibited high insertion losses, a minimum of 4.7 dB for the filter and 4.2 dB for the diplexer. Surface polishing and plating is required to reduce the high losses.

articleTitle: Substrate Integrated Waveguide Multiband Bandpass Filters and Multiplexers
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE MTT-S International Microwave Filter Workshop (IMFW)
abstract: The implementation schemes and techniques of substrate integrated waveguide (SIW) multiband bandpass filters (BPFs) and multiplexers are examined and summarized in this article. A comprehensive overview of technical approaches and diverse design methodologies are briefly described, basically embracing numerous schemes such as shunting, multimode resonator, multimode-shunting hybrid, and splitting structures.

articleTitle: Reconfigurable Bandpass Filter Using SLCFET Technology
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE MTT-S International Microwave Filter Workshop (IMFW)
abstract: We report on the successful fabrication and demonstration of a low loss, high performance reconfigurable bandpass filter technology. A digitally reconfigurable bandpass filter was implemented by placing the low pass and high pass reconfigurable filters in series. Reconfigurable low pass and high pass filters were implemented by combining MMICs with RF switches selecting capacitor values and off chip high Q fixed inductors. The same circuitry was implemented in both a commercial GaAs pHEMT process as well as Northrop Grumman’s GaN based SLCFET technology. The resulting reconfigurable bandpass filter operates between 1.0-2.0 GHz, with over 500 different filters selections and supporting variable center frequencies as well as variable bandwidth sizes ranging from 70 MHz to 100 MHz, all in a single device. Depending on the center frequency and bandwidth of the selected path, the SLCFET based switched reconfigurable filters demonstrated a NF and insertion loss improvement over the GaAs variant by > 2 dB, while demonstrating an P1dB<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">average</inf> of 33.6 dBm, compared to an average P1dB<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">average</inf>= 17.8 dBm power handling of the GaAs reconfigurable filter. The SLCFET based filter was measured as having 20x greater linearity than the GaAs filter, with the average two tone IIP3 for the SLCFET filter at 43 dBm, compared to 30 dBm for the GaAs design.

articleTitle: Evanescent mode filters composed of dielectric parts built using 3D-printing methods
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE MTT-S International Microwave Filter Workshop (IMFW)
abstract: In this work, two different types of evanescent mode rectangular waveguides filters are proposed, designed and fabricated, using a hybrid manufacturing strategy. On the one hand, the evanescent waveguide filter section is filled with dielectric material made of ABSplus, commonly employed by 3D printers based on Fused Deposition Modeling (FDM). On the other hand, the metallic external structure of the filters has been built by means of standard machining computer numerical control (CNC) procedures. Some guidelines on how to properly combine the dielectric and metallic pieces are provided. As design examples, two different fifth order C-band Chebyshev bandpass filters have been designed and tested. The first filter is composed of a single ABSplus dielectric piece (ϵ<inf>r</inf> = 2.55) drilled with elliptical airholes, and then aligned in the metallic waveguide housing. The second filter is loaded with five elliptical dielectric post resonators distributed along the metallic evanescent waveguide section. In both cases, the return losses are higher than RL = 18 dB, the fractional bandwidth within the range 3%-4.6%, whereas the spurious free range is around 1 GHz. Due to the nowadays limitations of the quality of available dielectric materials for 3D-printers, the insertion losses of the filters are high within the passbands (around IL = 4.3 dB). Nevertheless, the overall performances are satisfactory, showing the promising usefulness of this kind of filters for low cost implementations, based on combining additive manufacturing techniques with standard CNC processes.

articleTitle: Compact Cross-Coupled Bandpass Filter with Wide Stopband and Low Radiation Loss Using SIDGS
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE MTT-S International Microwave Filter Workshop (IMFW)
abstract: In this paper, a compact cross-coupled bandpass filter (BPF) with wide stopband and low radiation loss is proposed based on the substrate integrated defected ground structure (SIDGS). The SIDGS resonator can miniaturize the circuit size, reduce the radiation loss, and suppress the harmonics, simultaneously. To achieve the filtering response with wide stopband, three coupled SIDGS resonators with discrepant harmonic positions are used. Besides, an additional weak coupling path is introduced to generate a transmission zero at upper stopband. To verify the mechanism, a compact three-order BPF operating at 2.62 GHz (i.e., f<inf>0</inf>) is implemented and fabricated. Measured stopband bandwidth is up to 26 GHz (i.e., 9.92f<inf>0</inf>) with a rejection level higher than 27 dB.

articleTitle: Inline Generalized Chebyshev Dielectric Waveguide Filters With Nonlinear Frequency-Variant Inverters
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE MTT-S International Microwave Filter Workshop (IMFW)
abstract: This work presents the design techniques to realize highly compact inline generalized Chebyshev dielectric waveguide filters based on novel nonlinear frequency-variant coupling (NFVC) inverters. The discontinuities in the form of a pair of metalized blind holes placed at half-wavelength intervals in the broad wall of a rectangular dielectric waveguide operate as NFVC inverters. The NFVC produces a transmission pole in between a pair of fully controllable transmission zeros (TZs). The pole is added to the passband to increase the order of the filter without augmenting its physical volume. The simulated results for 3<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">rd</sup> and 5<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">th</sup> order inline dielectric waveguide filters with quasi-elliptic-type filtering response are presented to validate the design theory.

articleTitle: A novel Re-entrant Cap Tuning Technique For TM-Mode Dielectric Resonators and Filters
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE MTT-S International Microwave Filter Workshop (IMFW)
abstract: This paper reports a new tuning technique for TM mode dielectric resonators and filters. The proposed concept is based on the use of a hollow envelope (cap) to tune the resonant frequency instead of/in addition to the conventional intruding screw/rod-based method. The presented technique provides highly desirable advantages of tunable components including the wider tuning capabilities, simple configuration, high-power compatibility, and the improved Q factor. For proof of concept purposes, a tunable resonator is designed, fabricated, and measured. Also, a comparison with the conventional tuning technique is presented. The measured results demonstrate a wide tunability > 90% with a high Q-factor up to 3119 promoting the application of the proposed mechanism in high-performance tunable components.

articleTitle: Tx/Rx Diplexer for High-power Space Applications based on TM010 mode dielectric resonators
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE MTT-S International Microwave Filter Workshop (IMFW)
abstract: In this paper the most recent results concerning the design of very compact Tx/Rx L-band diplexers for high-power space applications are presented. Dielectric resonators based on TM<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">010</inf> mode have been chosen as the best compromise in terms of compactness and unloaded Q-factor (>2000). Geometries and materials of the diplexer have been selected in order to improve the performance in terms of power-handling, multipactor and PIM. In order to increase the isolation between the diplexer channels, transmission zeros generated by exploiting cross-coupled resonators have been used. Some cross-coupling mechanisms have already been proposed in previous papers, however measurements demonstrate that the manufacturing accuracy of such structures is much lower than required. In this document, an alternative solution is proposed.

articleTitle: Additive Manufacturing of Non-homogenous Dielectric Waveguide Structures and Filters
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE MTT-S International Microwave Filter Workshop (IMFW)
abstract: This paper investigates the use of 3D-printed alumina ceramics to achieve variable dielectric constants for novel microwave applications. An introduction to lithography-based ceramic manufacturing exhibits the novel process and material properties, while detailing printing techniques for achieving gradient and equivalent dielectric constants. Printed samples of non-homogeneous dielectrics are presented and briefly discussed. Potential end-use for microwave components are discussed with emphasis on future filter applications.

articleTitle: Millimeter-Wave CMOS Passive Filters for 5G Applications
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE MTT-S International Microwave Filter Workshop (IMFW)
abstract: Different types of RF passive-integrated wide-band bandpass filters (BPFs) and bandstop filters (BSFs) in CMOS technology that operate at the millimeter-wave region are presented. Firstly, the use of integrated 3-D inductors that exploit their parasitic capacitance to functionalize as LC tanks is shown. They enable highly-miniaturized on-chip wide-band BPF design as a result of the 3-D structure, along with transmission-zero (TZ) creation in the BPF response. Afterwards, a class of on-chip BSFs based on broadside-coupled meandered-line resonating cells is reported. Simulated and measured results of various built proof-of-concept RF-CMOS chips of the addressed BPF and BSF concepts are provided. These families of passive-integrated RF filtering components may find application in future wireless-communication radio systems as 5G.

articleTitle: Silver-Plated Dielectric Waveguide Filters Using Dual-Ridge Dual-Mode Resonator
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE MTT-S International Microwave Filter Workshop (IMFW)
abstract: In this design, two novel silver-plated dielectric waveguide filters with flexible transmission zeros are presented. The dual-mode dielectric resonator, which is based on TM<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">120</inf> and TM<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">210</inf> mode, consists of two ridges located at the center of the side wall. The resonant frequencies can be controlled by the lengths of the ridges. The intracavity coupling is achieved by a combination of a blind hole and a coupling iris. By changing the cascaded position of the two dual-ridge dual-mode resonators, different coupling topology can be obtained, and thus one or two transmission zeros can be set at the high end of the passband to improve the selectivity of the filter.

articleTitle: Additive manufacturing of a 4th-order K-band semi-planar slow-wave filter
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE MTT-S International Microwave Filter Workshop (IMFW)
abstract: This paper presents the exploitation of the additive manufacturing (AM) technique laser powder bed fusion (L-PBF), for the fabrication of a K-band meta-substrate filter. The decisions made through each round of prototyping are discussed. It also presents the crucial parameters that can lead to a higher quality end product of AM. The filter response and out-of-band performance are also discussed in short.

articleTitle: A Planar Quad-band Band-Pass Filter Employing Dual-Mode Band-Stop Resonators
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE MTT-S International Microwave Filter Workshop (IMFW)
abstract: A compact split-type quad-band band-pass filter employing dual-mode stub-load band-stop resonators is presented in this paper. The basic coupling schematic is originated from frequency transformation methods. Then, a dual-mode band-stop resonator, which can provide two controllable transmission zeros, is employed to replace the two single-mode band-stop resonators to achieve the same response. The filter has been synthesized, designed and simulated in planar microstrip technology to demonstrate the feasibility of the proposal. Comparing with filters based on single-mode resonators. This solution provides a relatively compact footprint, which features an attractive solution for filters’ miniaturization.

articleTitle: Compact G-CPW Fed Air-Filled SIW (AFSIW) Filters For Systems on Substrate
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE MTT-S International Microwave Filter Workshop (IMFW)
abstract: This paper presents the investigation and demonstration of novel compact grounded coplanar waveguide (G-CPW) fed air-filled substrate integrated waveguide (AFSIW) filters. The proposed topology implements input and output feedings from the top layer of the multilayer printed circuit board (PCB) that is used in microwave and millimeter-wave circuits and systems to host surface mount devices such as MMICs, which are interconnected using G-CPW or microstrip lines. In this purpose, the top substrate is typically a thin substrate implementing on its top G-CPW lines to minimize radiation and couplings compared to microstrip lines. In the proposed topology, coupling windows are etched on the top substrate ground to create the input and output couplings of the AFSIW filter. The design of the proposed AFSIW filter, which is of high interest for systems on substrate (SoS), is presented in detail. For demonstration purposes, a fourth order AFSIW filter operating at 21 GHz with a 325 MHz (1.55 %) bandwidth is designed, fabricated and measured. The results obtained in measurements are in good agreement with the simulations. The fabricated filter exhibits an insertion loss of 0.99 dB and an unloaded Q-factor of 1157.

articleTitle: Towards a N77 Electroacoustic Filter Using Thin Films of Crystalline Y-cut Lithium Niobate
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE MTT-S International Microwave Filter Workshop (IMFW)
abstract: This paper presents the use of a novel type of resonators made of a thin membrane of Y-cut Lithium Niobate that has an array of interdigitated electrodes on the top, and a floating metal on the bottom. Each electrode gives rise to a quasi-independent resonator and the shear waves can be properly excited. We use this novel resonator concept to design two filters at 3GHz central frequency and a bandwidth of 400MHz (13% relative) and 600MHz (20% relative), respectively. We believe this type of resonator will enable n77 bands filters.

articleTitle: T-shaped Dual-Mode Waveguide Filters with Low Manufacturing Complexity for mm-Wave Applications
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE MTT-S International Microwave Filter Workshop (IMFW)
abstract: This paper presents a novel T-shaped dual-mode waveguide resonator. Each resonator introduces one transmission zero (TZ) to the frequency response, either below or above the passband. The position of the TZ depends on the resonance frequencies of both resonant modes. Field evaluations of the modes as well as parameter studies are accomplished within this paper. Two fourth order filters in the D-band (110-170 GHz, WR-6) are subsequently realized as proof of concept with the classical computer numerical control (CNC) milling technique. Both filters realize a similar filter response but have a different mechanical cutting plane, which has a large influence on the manufacturability and hence on the measurement results.

articleTitle: Self Cancellation of Higher Order Mode Spurious Frequencies in SIW Filters
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE MTT-S International Microwave Filter Workshop (IMFW)
abstract: In this paper, a new approach for the suppression of higher order mode spurious frequencies in SIW filters is proposed. The proposed structure is a double layer SIW filter. In this structure, all couplings related to the higher order modes generating the spurious frequencies are maximized with the exception of the central one that is instead minimized. This higher order mode coupling configuration allows for removing the spurious through a self-cancellation mechanism, in which spurious contributions cancel one another. In this approach, the only iris that need to be designed in order to minimize the coupling to the higher order mode is the central one, that is the iris between the two layers. This approach has been compared with a classical one in which spurious couplings are minimized as much as possible. In the classical approach, all irises should be as our central iris, resulting in a multilayer structure in which each layer contains a single resonator only. In this paper, it is demonstrated that the new approach has the advantage of being more effective in spurious suppression and it has an easier manufacturing. The two approaches have been compared through the design of 4<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">th</sup> order filters. The filter based on the new method has been manufactured and measured, thus demonstrating the feasibility of the proposed approach.

articleTitle: 5G C-V2X Filter Using BAW Technology
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE MTT-S International Microwave Filter Workshop (IMFW)
abstract: A new spectrum of frequencies are allotted for next generation wireless communication systems based on 5G. Bulk acoustic wave (BAW) filters are well poised to support the new 5G radio-bands and beyond. This report presents an overview of BAW filter development for high frequency bands, design challenges and integration complexities. In addition, the feasibility of BAW technology for high frequency applications is demonstrated through a 5.9 GHz filter.

articleTitle: Satellite Filters for 5G/6G and Beyond
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE MTT-S International Microwave Filter Workshop (IMFW)
abstract: Legacy satellite communication systems offered limited integration with terrestrial networks, mainly due to commercial and technological biases. With the satellite element now becoming part of the 5G ecosystem, it is expected that evolutions in the ground and space segments will inevitably impact the role of microwave filters into the new systems. This paper describes applications of filter technology in the context of satellite-terrestrial 5G communications and provides an overview of potential challenges and opportunities.

articleTitle: Substrate-Integrated-Waveguide Diplexer Filter for SATCOM-on-the-Move
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE MTT-S International Microwave Filter Workshop (IMFW)
abstract: Satellite communication (SATCOM) on-the-move applications require low-cost compact antenna arrays to enable mobile users to track the satellites. Full-duplex operation requires efficient diplexers that satisfy stringent requirements in a compact footprint to enable tight integration within the antenna system. In this contribution, substrate-integrated-waveguide technology is leveraged to design a single-layer third-order diplexer filter based on a dual-mode cavity. Simulations and measurements demonstrate that the diplexer enables full-duplex operation for Ku-band SATCOM on-the-move systems, effectively separating the [11.7-12.75] GHz downlink (Rx) band from the [13.75-14.50] GHz uplink (Tx) band, yielding an isolation larger than 20 dB and an insertion loss below 3.7 dB over a fractional bandwidth (FBW) of 8.6% in Rx and 5.3% in Tx.

articleTitle: Non-Reciprocal Bandpass Filter with Tunable Center Frequency and Constant Fractional Bandwidth
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE MTT-S International Microwave Filter Workshop (IMFW)
abstract: This paper presents a novel frequency reconfigurable microstrip non-reciprocal bandpass filter (BPF) with constant fractional bandwidth (FBW) based on time modulated λg/4 stepped impedance coupled-line resonators (SICLRs). The modulation is achieved by loading both ends of the λg/4 resonators with varactor diodes. By modulating the resonant frequencies of the filter’s resonators with phase shifted AC signals, the forward and backward waves can be controlled. In this manner, RF propagation is enabled in one direction (from port 1 to port 2), having the backward wave sufficiently attenuated. In addition, changing the resonant frequencies of the filter’s resonators, the center frequency can be tuned keeping the FBW constant. A two-pole BPF was designed, fabricated and measured demonstrating 1.34:1 center frequency tuning in the non-reciprocal state whereas the reverse isolation was measured up to 29 dB.

articleTitle: Millimeter-Wave Dual-Polarized Filtering Antenna Design for 5G AiP Application
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE MTT-S International Microwave Filter Workshop (IMFW)
abstract: This paper presents a design method of dual-polarized millimeter-wave (mm-Wave) filtering antenna with high selectivity. The proposed antenna design consists of a differential-fed driven patch and stacked parasitic structures. The combination of the stacked structures and the driven patch can be equivalent to band-stop filtering circuits for generating radiation nulls at the stopband. Besides, additional shorted patches as band-stop structures are embedded into the driven patch for introducing other radiation nulls at the band-edges. As a result, a quasi-elliptic bandpass response is realized without requiring extra filtering circuit. Based on the above design method, two different mm-Wave filtering antennas with high roll-off rate are proposed. Both of them can be fabricated with low-cost PCB process. These merits make the proposed antenna design a good candidate for the 5G mm-Wave antenna-in-package (AiP) application to reduce the requirements of the filters in the mm-Wave RF frontends.

articleTitle: Recent Advances in Multiphysics Optimization for Microwave Filters Using Space Mapping Techniques
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE MTT-S International Microwave Filter Workshop (IMFW)
abstract: Multiphysics analysis, which involves the EM domain with other physics domains, is increasingly important for high-performance microwave components to obtain an accurate system design. This paper provides an overview of the recent advances in multiphysics optimization using space mapping techniques. A space-mapping-based surrogate model including an EM domain coarse model and two mapping functions is presented. By exploiting the knowledge of the coarse model established by relatively inexpensive EM data, this technique can provide a larger and more efficient optimization update in each optimization iteration, consequently obtaining optimal solutions faster than the existing multiphysics optimization without space mapping. A high power microwave filter is used to illustrate this technique.

articleTitle: Extended Path Filter Configurations
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE MTT-S International Microwave Filter Workshop (IMFW)
abstract: In this work we introduce a method for increasing the maximum number of transmission zeros in the response of path filters. This recently introduced inline filter configuration allows for up to four transmission zeros on the imaginary axis. The solution proposed in this work, while maintaining the inline configuration, increases the number of transmission zeros up to N-1 (with N order of the filter). The novel concept allowing the additional zeros introduction is verified by means of the design of a waveguide filter of order 8 with 6 transmission zeros.

articleTitle: Miniaturized Ultra-Wideband Bandpass Filter Based on Substrate Integrated Quasi-Lumped Resonators
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE MTT-S International Microwave Filter Workshop (IMFW)
abstract: A compact ultra-wideband bandpass filter employing substrate integrated quasi-lumped resonators is presented in this paper. A multi-layer hybrid structure is proposed, combining quasi-lumped resonators and surface mount components. This allows a huge miniaturization degree due to the high capacitive loading. Moreover, strong magnetic and electric couplings can be implemented thus enabling the introduction of transmission zeros for improving response selectivity. A filter example centered at 5.35 GHz with a prescribed channel bandwidth of 2.9 GHz has been designed, manufactured and measured. The filter size is smaller than 7×7 mm<sup>2</sup>. The obtained results show the feasibility of the proposed approach.

articleTitle: On the Influence of Input Phase on the Allocation of Transmission Zeros in Acoustic Ladder Filters
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE MTT-S International Microwave Filter Workshop (IMFW)
abstract: This work presents a novel concept in the design of acoustic wave ladder filters: using a series resonator to place a transmission zero below the passband. Moving transmission zeros from above to below the passband, or vice versa, is feasible by careful consideration of the filter reflection phase and allows to go beyond the traditional ladder concept in the design of acoustic wave filters with alternating transmission zeros. The method is faced from a rigorous and accurate synthesis perspective and provides the key aspects that lead to the novel solution for performing alternative responses. Filter examples with evenly distributed coupling coefficient among resonators are provided and compared with a traditional filter alternating zeros above and below the passband. The proposed approach can be specially exploited to enhance filter selectivity or improve out-of-band rejection, while also allowing to keep appropriate impedance ratios among all resonators.

articleTitle: Compact Dual-Band Bandpass Filter with Wide Stopband Using Hybrid Microstrip/DGS
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE MTT-S International Microwave Filter Workshop (IMFW)
abstract: In this paper, a dual-band bandpass filter (BPF) with wide stopband is proposed based on hybrid microstrip/defected ground structure (DGS). Such hybrid microstrip/DGS structure consists of stepped-impedance DGS on the bottom layer and microstrip stepped-impedance resonators (SIRs) on the top layer. Meanwhile, the spurious could be suppressed by separated harmonic locations of stepped-impedance DGS and microstrip SIRs, which leads to a wide stopband response. To verify the mechanisms, a dual-band BPF centered at 2.39 and 5.30 GHz is implemented and fabricated. The measured results show that the stopband exhibits more than 14.6 times of the first resonance with rejection level higher than 20 dB.

articleTitle: An Ultra-Low Impedance 4.8 GHz Al72Sc28N Resonant Rods Resonator With a Record kt2 of 21.2%
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE MTT-S International Microwave Filter Workshop (IMFW)
abstract: This work reports on the measured performance of the first Aluminum Scandium Nitride Two-Dimensional Resonant Rods resonator (2DRR) fabricated using a Sc-doping concentration of 28% (i.e. Al72Sc28N), characterized by an ultra-low impedance (~12 Ω), and exhibiting an all-time record electromechanical coupling coefficient ($k_t^2$) of 21.2%. Due to its unprecedented $k_t^2$, enabled by its unique dispersion characteristics, the reported 2DRR opens exciting scenarios towards the development of next generation monolithic integrated radio-frequency (RF) filtering components. In particular, given the demonstrated electromechanical performance of the reported 2DRR device, we show that 2DRR-based ladder filters with ~9.2% of fractional bandwidth, ~2.5 dB insertion-loss (I.L) and a >40 dB out-of-band rejection can be envisioned in the short-term, providing unprecedented means to extend the commercial and military use of acoustic filters up to the mm-wave frequency range.

articleTitle: Filtering In-Band Full-Duplex Slot Antenna Based on TM120 and TM210 Dual-Mode Resonators
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE MTT-S International Microwave Filter Workshop (IMFW)
abstract: A filtering in-band full-duplex (IBFD) cavity-backed slot antenna is presented in this paper. Each of channels in the full-duplex function is dominated by a pair of degenerate modes, namely TM210 and TM120, respectively. High isolation can be implemented between channels due to the modal orthogonality of degenerate modes. In the filtering function, both channels share the common cavity resonators from the first order to the last order with specified external quality factors (Q<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">e</inf>) and coupling coefficient (K). At the last order, radiating slots for both channels are adopted to transmit/receive the dual-polarized signals, respectively. For proof-of-concept, a 2<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">nd</sup>-order IBFD slot antenna prototype is constructed and simulated. It resonates at 10 GHz with a fractional bandwidth of 3.3% and a realized gain of 10. 3 dBi.

articleTitle: Planar Balanced Filters with Ultrawide Band Common-mode Suppression and Tunable Notch
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE MTT-S International Microwave Filter Workshop (IMFW)
abstract: An ultra-wideband differential filter with common-mode suppression over the whole band is presented. To this end, a pair of back-to-back balanced microstrip-to-slotline transitions are utilized. It is demonstrated that due to the electric wall at the symmetry plane of the structure, which is only available for differential excitation, strong coupling, and, as a result, a UWB bandpass behavior for differential signals is achieved. In contrast, the structure strongly rejects common-mode signals. It is further shown that different types of unbalanced filters can be integrated with the proposed structure, thus achieving elaborate frequency responses while avoiding the complexities associated with balanced filter design.

articleTitle: Design of Filtering Rat-race Coupler Based on Hemispherical Resonator
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE MTT-S International Microwave Filter Workshop (IMFW)
abstract: In this paper, a novel filtering rat-race coupler based on hemispherical cavity resonator is proposed for the first time. It is designed in dual-cavities configuration by utilizing dual-mode high Q-factor hemispherical cavity and four feeding probes. Without an additional circuit, the prescribed 0° and 180° phase differences of this filtering coupler are realized by the in-phase and out-of-phase characteristics of E-fields at TM<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">201</inf> and its degenerate mode of the hemispherical cavity. By elaborately arranging the location of ports and coupling slots, magnitude and phase properties of the filtering rat-race coupler topology are easily attained. Compared with other reported filtering coupler, the proposed design exhibits many advantages including compact size, high Q-factor, and good filtering responses. For validation, the performance of the proposed hemispherical filtering coupler is demonstrated by simulation results.

articleTitle: A Miniature UWB Filter with In-Band Interference Cancelation
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE MTT-S International Microwave Filter Workshop (IMFW)
abstract: This paper presents a design for a miniature filter that can be configured as either an ultra-wideband (UWB) filter or a UWB band filter with in-band rejection for interference cancelation. A microstrip filter with N resonators is integrated with N+1 lumped capacitors to effectively produce 2N+1 resonators. With the proper choice of the resonator dimensions and the lumped element capacitors values, the filter can be configured as UWB filter with an order of 2N+1 or as a filter, with a dual-band response having one band of order N+1 and the other band of order N, with an isolation guard band in-between to eliminate interference. EM theoretical and measured results are presented to verify the validity of the concept.

articleTitle: Filter Model Extraction with Convolutional Neural Network Based on Magnitude Information
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE MTT-S International Microwave Filter Workshop (IMFW)
abstract: In this paper, a new model extraction method for band-pass filters with convolutional neural network (CNN) based on magnitude information only is introduced. A data augmentation approach and a data decentralization process to improve the CNN model performance by statistical analysis are proposed. A correction process utilizing real test data is introduced to improve the model performance. Compared to the existing model extraction method, this CNN model approach needs no phase information that is highly dependent on the loading circuit of a filter. Merely using the magnitude information, a good fitness for the response of high-order filters with complicated topology is achieved with this method. CNN model demonstrates a faster convergence compared to the traditional fully connected neural model.

articleTitle: A reconfigurable dual-mode Filter in Embedded Suspended Stripline Substrate Technology (ESSS)
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE MTT-S International Microwave Filter Workshop (IMFW)
abstract: A new configuration of embedded suspended stripline in PCB is proposed where a direct copper-to-copper connection joins the metalized cavity walls with the ground layer. The proposed stack-up has the advantage of an increased shielding compared to stack-ups based on via walls. A dual-mode filter demonstrator is designed and realized with discrete frequency tunability. The designed filter frequency is set around 30.5 GHz where the insertion loss (IL) is 1.06 dB and the Fractional Bandwidth (FBW) is 10.3%. The resonant frequency can be tuned to 29.60 GHz using a hardwired switch for a proof of concept. The realized prototype measurements show a good agreement between simulated and measured filters response.

articleTitle: Compact One-piece Coaxial In-line Comb Filters and Duplexers with Transmission Zeros
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE MTT-S International Microwave Filter Workshop (IMFW)
abstract: This paper introduces a specific class of in-line coaxial pass-band filters that do not require explicit cross couplings for the realization of transmission zeros. Both lower stopband and upper stopband TZs can be accommodated in the frequency response. The resulting structure is a compact one-piece metal filter or diplexer that can find application in low-loss, low PIM applications.

articleTitle: Experimental Evaluation of Dielectric-filled SIW Filter Continuous Wave Power Handling
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE MTT-S International Microwave Filter Workshop (IMFW)
abstract: In this paper, an experimental evaluation of the continuous wave power handling of dielectric-filled SIW filters is reported. First, the evaluated 400 MHz bandwidth four-pole dielectric-filled SIW filter centred at 21.4 GHz and based on 0.508 mm thick 6002 Rogers substrate is presented with its small signal measurement using a WR51 test fixture specially designed to handle high-power test. Then, the four-pole filter is tested using the test fixture in atmospheric conditions at ambient temperature and continuous wave power. It is shown that the evaluated four-pole filter was able to handle as much as 100 W of continuous wave power before destruction. To the author’s best knowledge, such experimental evaluation has never been reported in the literature, mainly because conventional dielectric-filled SIW is not intended for high-power applications. However, with the emergence of new threats, especially for military and space microwave systems, it becomes important to assess the power handling limitation of SIW components and circuits.

articleTitle: Effects of non-identical resonators on BAW linearity
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE MTT-S International Microwave Filter Workshop (IMFW)
abstract: Nonlinear (NL) performance requirements on BAW filters and modules became increasingly stringent in the past years. Common layout strategies efficiently help to improve the overall level for H2 and IMD. However, nowadays ambitious performance targets reveal the limits of common linearization approaches on real BAW filters and modules. The prediction from electro-magnetic (EM) simulation is remarkably accurate regarding the overall level. However, usually resonators using the same layer stack and geometry are considered perfectly identical in simulation regarding their resonance frequency and spurious content, neglecting the effect of natural process variation present on a real chip. In this article, the effect of imperfect, non-identical resonators is demonstrated, focusing especially on the deteriorated NL cancellation of cascaded or antiparallel stages. An overview is given of how different variation effects manifest in the NL response and methods to analyse the measured data are presented.

articleTitle: Investigation of a 3D-Printed Narrowband Filter with Non-Resonating Nodes
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE MTT-S International Microwave Filter Workshop (IMFW)
abstract: In this paper a narrowband third-order filter at 9 GHz with two transmission zeros is designed using the non-resonating node (NRN) method. The filter is fabricated using selective laser melting (SLM) technology. Without tuning, the measurements show promising results, but with a frequency shift and resonator detuning. Micro X-Ray CT imaging has been performed to investigate the imperfection in the manufacture. Dimension measurement of the structure show the level of dimension offset and some evidence of excessive shrinkage from the small iris structures.

articleTitle: RF Transceiver with Antenna Design for Ultra-wide Band Applications
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE MTT-S International Microwave Filter Workshop (IMFW)
abstract: The proposed article introduces RF wireless integrated transceiver for ulra-wideband wireless applications. The proposed wireless integrated transmitter consists of two-stage power amplifier (PA) with pre-distorter, band-pass Gm-C filter, distributed single-pole double-throw (SPDT) radio frequency (RF) switching, low noise amplifier (LNA) with balun and antenna design. The presented PA design presents conversion gain of 12.8 dB, the output 1-dB compression point (OP <inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1dB</inf> ) of -1.3 dBm and power added efficiency (PAE) higher than 3.04%, respectively. The presented LNA presents return loss of input higher than 10.32 dB, return loss of output higher than 10.77 dB, the exhibits gain from 8.16 to 13.1 dB, isolation higher than 42 dB, the exhibits noise figure from 4.48 to 7.66 dB, the exhibits input 1-dB compression point (IP <inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1dB</inf> ) from -13.43 to -5.43 dB, respectively. The implemented integrated transmitter using 0.18um CMOS technology has experimental outdoor/ indoor throughput base on channels, distance and concurrently complies with the Bluetooth wireless requirement.

articleTitle: Planar and Low-consumption Switchable Filter Banks with Tunable Passband and Stopband Responses
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE MTT-S International Microwave Filter Workshop (IMFW)
abstract: This paper presents the first experimental results of planar and low-consumption switchable stopband and passband filter banks. The channels are based on microstrip reconfigurable filters with wide tuning range. The devices are properly designed for wideband applications in the range of 2GHz÷18GHz and DC÷18GHz. The Switchable and tunable sub-bands are selected by means of digitally controlled switching matrices. In both cases high-Q varactor diodes are used to tune the frequency of the filters. The measured rejection of the stopband filter bank in the notched bands of 500÷600MHz is above 35dBc. The overall volume is within 70x50x10mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup> and the maximum power consumption is below 1.5W. The measured insertion loss flatness of the passband filter bank channels is lower than 3dB and the out-of-band attenuation is over 45dBc. The overall footprint is within 100x190x25mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup> and the maximum power consumption is below 4W.

articleTitle: Four-Port Multiband MIMO Filtenna with an Isolation Filter for Sub-6 GHz 5G Applications
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE MTT-S International Microwave Filter Workshop (IMFW)
abstract: In this paper, a four-port multiple-input-multiple-output (MIMO) filtenna (antenna with filter) system with isolation enhancing band-reject filter (BRF) is presented. The filtenna system is designed by integrating a multi-functional filter (MFF) in the antenna’s feed line. The MFF has two modes of operation. In its 1<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">st</sup> mode, the filtenna system acts as a dualband antenna in the frequency range of 2.3-4.5 GHz and 5.3-5.5 GHz. While, in the 2<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">nd</sup> mode, it acts as a single band antenna in the frequency range 3.3-4.1 GHz. To improve the isolation between the antenna elements, an open stub line (OSL) based BRF has been incorporated in the ground plane of the filtenna system. The overall design is integrated into a Rogers RO 4003C substrate (ε<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">r</inf>=3.55, tanδ=0.0031) of dimension 100×65×1.52 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>. The designed antenna system is suitable for sub-6 GHz fifth-generation (5G) systems.

articleTitle: Extraction Techniques for Generic Cascaded Synthesis
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE MTT-S International Microwave Filter Workshop (IMFW)
abstract: The aim of this paper is to demonstrate that extraction techniques can be efficiently combined with coupling matrix synthesis techniques. An extension of a recently presented method based on a functional decomposition of the scattering matrix is introduced in order to add dangling resonators based on non resonating nodes among possible buildings blocks. This leads to a complete analytical procedure for hybrid realisations including classical N-tuplets, frequency depending couplings, constant phase shifts and NRNs. After detailing some elementary concepts of functional extraction techniques for NRN’s, a synthesis and design example is presented to illustrate the approach.

articleTitle: Advanced CEM Codes for Microwave Synthesis: Full-Wave Coupling Matrix in Electromagnetics
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE MTT-S International Microwave Filter Workshop (IMFW)
abstract: Electromagnetics today underpins all modern information and communication technologies. Increasing deployment of telecommunication services is urging RF industry to carry out better and better electrical designs, where a single device is no longer conceived to perform a single functionality, but rather multiple tasks at the same time.Unfortunately, much electrical design activity is still based on brute-force computational simulations to predict the actual physical behavior of electromagnetic devices. These time-consuming simulations are repeated, changing the device characteristics until satisfying stricter specifications of emerging information and communications technologies (5G and IoT).In our work we use computational electromagnetics as an actual design tool, rather than just an analysis one. This can be achieved by shriking computational electromagnetics into a simple parameterized equivalent circuit form, from which an electrical engineer can get actionable design insights.

articleTitle: Compact Filtering Power Divider with Distributed Combline Coupled-Resonators
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE MTT-S International Microwave Filter Workshop (IMFW)
abstract: In this communication, we present a compact single-layer filtering power divider in substrate integrated waveguide technology. The distributed combline resonators are effectively adopted to form a power divider with Chebyshev filtering response. The etched capacitive annular gaps and TEM-based combline resonators enable a miniaturized and tunable power divider design, with low-cost PCB-based fabrication. For demonstration, a fourth-degree four-way power divider operating at X-band is designed and fabricated. The simulation and experimental results are in good agreement and exhibit excellent selectivity performance alongside with a 50% size reduction.

articleTitle: Dimensioning Criteria for TE<inf>201</inf> Waveguide Singlet
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE MTT-S International Microwave Filter Workshop (IMFW)
abstract: In this work we introduce dimensioning criteria for waveguide singlets based on TE201 resonating cavities. By means of an ‘ad hoc’ developed mode matching software, suitable charts have been prepared to identify the proper combination of the singlet geometrical parameters allowing to obtain the desired values for the equivalent circuit extracted elements. The subsequent refinement can be carried out very quickly being the identified starting point relatively accurate. The proposed procedure allows a noticeable reduction of the time required for dimensioning extracted-pole filters employing the considered singlets.

articleTitle: Quasi-reflection-less bandpass filter with a variable frequency plan
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE MTT-S International Microwave Filter Workshop (IMFW)
abstract: An adjustable blueprint of microwave quasireflection-less band pass filter is presented in this article in order to execute multiple filter responses with the same design. A three-channel quasi-reflection-less filter is considered and a combination between different bands is achieved by combining channels together while maintaining a quasi-reflection-less particularity. The addition of RF switches with variable states insure the overall resilience of the final design by insuring tunable bands and answer the rising need of complex specifications without incrementing the congestion. The complexity of this design can be pushed further by increasing the number and order of the filters along with the quantity of RF switch and accordingly retrieve a higher number of possible configurations.

articleTitle: Design of a Compact, Highly-Integrated, Eight-Filter Module Using Multilayered-PCB
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE MTT-S International Microwave Filter Workshop (IMFW)
abstract: This paper proposes the design of a compact module integrating a set of eight bandpass filters, each one exhibiting a relative passband of 43%, with central frequencies spanning from 2.55 GHz up to 14.85 GHz. Electrical responses of the filters are optimized so that, apart from their passband, no spurious resonances appear within the 2-18 GHz frequency range. Compactness is achieved thanks to the stacking of the designed filters on several stages of a multilayer stack-up. Originality of this work relies on the combination of multilayered technology together with optimized topology (harmonic control, access transition) to achieve a compact yet electrically highly-performant module.

articleTitle: Resistorless Implementation of Lossy Filters Using Coaxial SIW Resonators With Non-uniform Q
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE MTT-S International Microwave Filter Workshop (IMFW)
abstract: A technique for designing bandpass filters with very flat amplitude response is presented in this paper. The approach is based on the use of non-uniform-Q resonators implemented in coaxial substrate integrated waveguide (SIW) technology. An important unloaded Q-factor ratio can be obtained by adequately controlling several layout parameters of the basic resonator cell, thus enabling to optimize the in-band response of the filter. The approach is experimentally demonstrated at X-band frequencies by designing two resonators in Rogers RO4003C (ϵ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">r</inf> = 3.55, tan δ = 0.0027) with unloaded Q-factors going from 53 to 270. Then, a 4th-order filter example with 2 transmission zeros is designed, fabricated and measured based on the former results. The filter is centered at 10 GHz with a 280 MHz bandwidth showing a in-band flatness better than 1 dB-pp, which would require an unloaded Q-factor about 600 for a uniform-Q implementation, therefore showing the advantages of the proposed approach for implementing bandpass filters for high-end RF and microwave applications.

articleTitle: Synthesis of 2-CRF Section Filter without External Elements
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE MTT-S International Microwave Filter Workshop (IMFW)
abstract: This paper presents the synthesis and circuit transformation for fourth-order filters based on two CRF sections. The synthesized network selects the input and output electro-acoustic couplings and defines the position of the four eigen modes excited in the topology. These values can be related with the physical dimensions of the structure. This is the area and layer configuration and thicknesses. The synthesis method reveals the existence of multiple solutions for a given filter response, which give rise to a different degree of miniaturization. Final simulated illustrative designs will be outlined to verify the synthesis method.

articleTitle: An Integrated Passive Device RF Front-End for Narrow-Band Internet-of-Things Modules
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE MTT-S International Microwave Filter Workshop (IMFW)
abstract: This paper presents an integrated passive device (IPD) solution, that implements a dedicated RF front-end (RF-FE) for narrow-band internet-of-things (NB-IoT) modules. Adopting ST-proprietary IPD technology it is possible to integrate in a unique device several stand-alone RF functions. In particular, a prototype embedding balun, low-pass filters and a coupler has been conceived, designed, and experimentally validated. In addition, this solution is highly versatile, providing compatibility with both the design of planar technology modules, molded modules and stacked modules, making it attractive for the implementation of the future generation of radio modules.

articleTitle: Reconfigurable Bandpass Filter with Extracted Pole and Coupling Resonators
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE MTT-S International Microwave Filter Workshop (IMFW)
abstract: This paper presents a reconfigurable bandpass filter with an extracted pole section in the Ku-band. The filter’s center frequency and bandwidth can be controlled independently from each other by using additional resonators. The center frequency can be varied between 13.8 GHz and 14.8 GHz while the bandwidth can be varied between 100 MHz and 200 MHz in the given center frequency range. The extracted pole section provides a transmission zero close to the passband, which increases the selectivity and remains in place relative to the passband during all tuning states.

articleTitle: Exhaustive Synthesis and Realization of Extended-Box Topologies With Dispersive Couplings
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE MTT-S International Microwave Filter Workshop (IMFW)
abstract: In this paper, an exhaustive general synthesis method is proposed for the extended-box topologies with dispersive couplings, which is very suitable for the realization of the monoblock dielectric resonator filters. The difficulty of introducing the diagonal cross coupling calls for the extended-box topology. When properly utilizing the inevitable dispersion effect of the negative coupling introduced by a metalized blind hole, an extra transmission zero generates. Multiple solutions can be observed by solving the polynomial equation system established based on the congruent transformation, from which the solution most suitable for realization can be selected and realized. A six-pole filter in extended-box topology with a dispersive coupling is synthesized and EM designed for validation.

articleTitle: ALD Stripline Resonator and Bandpass Filters for VHF and UHF Bands
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE MTT-S International Microwave Filter Workshop (IMFW)
abstract: It is shown that for an optimal substrate thickness ALD technology will be promising for IF bandpass filter designing. A two-conductor stripline ALD resonator with central frequency 200 MHz will have Q-factor 53 with total length 3.7 mm (0.0025λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">g</inf>) and the frequency separation of the first and the second oscillation modes up to 59. Two bandpass filters for VHF and UHF designed and fabricated for commercial application display good agreement between the simulation and the experiment. A 3-pole bandpass filter with central frequency 255 MHz and lateral size 15.8×3.2 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> has stopband width 13.5f<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf>, and a 6-pole bandpass filter with central frequency 1250 MHz and lateral size 4.4×5.1 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> has stopband width 9.4f<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf>.

articleTitle: A Slot Filtenna Based on Gap Waveguide Using Novel Sidewalls
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE MTT-S International Microwave Filter Workshop (IMFW)
abstract: This paper presents a cavity-backed slot filtering antenna (filtenna) designed based on gap waveguide structure using novel sidewalls. Rather than using traditional full-length pins, the unit-cell geometry of the proposed pin-form consists of a pin mounted on a solid wall, where the total height of the pin and wall is quarter wavelength of the operating frequency in free space. The resonant frequency of the designed filtenna is 30.5 GHz and the fractional bandwidth is 6.3%. The designed filtering antenna is fabricated using computer numerical control (CNC) milling technology. The simulated and measured results of the proposed filtenna are in excellent agreement.

articleTitle: On-Silicon efficient integrated DRAs for millimeter-wave energy harvesting solutions
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE MTT-S International Microwave Filter Workshop (IMFW)
abstract: This paper presents preliminary results of dielectric resonator antennas (DRAs), exploiting silicon, as possible candidates for compact energy harvesting system fully integrated on silicon. The antennas are designed to operate at 24 GHz using a 0.525-mm thick high resistivity silicon substrate. Different shapes and solutions are considered: first cylindrical and cuboid elements are characterized under the HEM<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11δ</inf> hybrid mode excitation and promising performance are demonstrated with a very good compromise between compactness and radiation performance: for a DRA with a volume as low as 7 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>, a radiation efficiency of 75% and a maximum gain of 4.72 dBi have been obtained. Subsequently, a millimeter-wave rectenna, based on the proposed DRA, is designed, providing an RF-to-dc conversion efficiency of 33% for a received power of 8 dBm, with a maximum output dc voltage of about 3V. Based on these designs a fully integrated 2 x 2 silicon array is realized, for enhancing the energy harvesting capabilities in the mmWave range, while preserving the compactness of the entire system. In this case, the maximum gain of the antenna is equal to 7.3 dBi with a radiation efficiency equal to 60%.

articleTitle: Effects of Cutting Planes on Filter Performance of FDM 3D-Printed X-Band Waveguide Filters
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE MTT-S International Microwave Filter Workshop (IMFW)
abstract: In this paper, the impact of E-plane and H-plane cuts on filter performance of 3D-printed waveguide filters manufactured with fused deposition modeling (FDM) is examined. The employed manufacturing procedure consists of FDM 3D-printing and the subsequent electroplating process. A number of samples in both configurations are fabricated and surveyed. The measurement results are quantified and a comparison is conducted. Finally, the differing filter behaviors are discussed.

articleTitle: Design of Dual/Tri-Band Filtering Antenna Using Multi-Mode SIW Cavities
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE MTT-S International Microwave Filter Workshop (IMFW)
abstract: Compact, vertically-integrated dual- and tri-band filtering antennas based on multi-mode substrate integrated waveguide (SIW) cavities are developed. The electric filed distributions of the resonant modes in a SIW cavity are firstly analyzed. And then, a dual-band SIW filtering antenna is developed by employing a dual-mode SIW cavity and a slot-loaded SIW cavity. In the dual-band design process, a SIW cavity, operating at its TE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">110</inf> and TE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">120</inf> modes, is utilized as the feeding cavity, and a slot-loaded SIW cavity is stacked over the dual-mode SIW feeding cavity to simultaneously realize the dual-band function and facilitate the filtering response for both two passbands. Finally, in order to achieve the tri-band function, a multi-mode SIW cavity, operating at its TE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">110</inf>, TE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">120</inf>, and TE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">210</inf> modes, is selected as the feeding cavity. According to properties of the electric field magnitude distributions of the three modes in SIW cavity, the position of the feeding line is elaborately designed to simultaneously excite these three modes. Likewise, a slot-loaded SIW cavity is employed to stack with the multi-mode SIW feeding cavity to accomplish the tri-band function and improve the frequency selectivity for three passbands. The simulated results demonstrate that both the dual-band and tri-band SIW filtering antennas possess good in-band and out-of-band performance characteristics.

articleTitle: Compact Filtering Antennas Based On Dual-Mode SIW Cavity
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE MTT-S International Microwave Filter Workshop (IMFW)
abstract: A brief review of compact filtering antennas (or filtennas) based on the dual-mode substrate integrated waveguide (SIW) cavity is presented in this paper. Three configurations are proposed to realize circularly polarized (CP), dual-polarized and dual-band filtennas, respectively. In these designs, four orthogonal half-mode (HM) patches serving as radiators are employed in conjunction with a dual-mode SIW cavity. Sparse vias are used as coupling windows between the SIW cavity and HM patches, while maintaining the original sharp dual-mode filtering response. Folded structures are applied to reduce the aperture size and form un-splitted radiation beams with small side lobes.

articleTitle: A Design Method of Wideband BPF Considering Frequency Dependence of Inverters for SAW Filter
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE MTT-S International Microwave Filter Workshop (IMFW)
abstract: In this paper, a band pass filter (BPF) design method considering the inverter’s frequency dependence is presented. In this method, the new admittance compensation method is added to the conventional method compensating for phase frequency variations. The proposed method efficiently improves the frequency shift and unwanted bandwidth when designing more than 20% of bandwidth, while the conventional method has frequency degradation at a 10% Fractional Bandwidth(FBW). The proposed design theory is verified by circuit simulation and measurement. The measured results show the improvement of 20MHz frequency shift and FBW. Furthermore, the proposed method is applied to the SAW Filter design method, and it is also approved that the frequency shift is compensated for when designing a 10% FBW.

articleTitle: Bandwidth-Reconfigurable Liquid-Metal Tunable Bandpass Filter
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE MTT-S International Microwave Filter Workshop (IMFW)
abstract: A bandwidth reconfigurable substrate integrated waveguide (SIW) filter utilizing liquid metal is presented. The design is implemented with two continuously tunable cavity resonators that are coupled together by a novel inductive iris design. For bandwidth control, five continuously tunable liquid metal posts are located in the inductive iris. Each via can be capacitively loaded with liquid metal to increase the inter-resonator coupling or short-circuited to reduce the effective iris width. The combination of capacitive loading and inductive shorting allows for a wide range of realizable bandwidths over the frequency tuning range of the device. Filter samples were fabricated, and the iris tuning mechanism was validated by realizing a 541 MHz Butterworth response and a 278 MHz Butterworth response by tuning the liquid metal in the five iris tuning posts.

articleTitle: Frequency Adjustable Narrow- and Moderate Bandwidth Filters with Wide Tuning Range
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE MTT-S International Microwave Filter Workshop (IMFW)
abstract: This work presents a compact (~25.3 – 34.0°) mechanically reconfigurable filter capable of wide tuning range (~30%) maintaining a stable fractional bandwidth. A common single tuning mechanism simplifies the design. The proposed technology is low-cost and implemented with low complexity. The filter maintains high Q factor across the range. Two distinct designs demonstrate the ability to implement this technology for narrow-band as well as wide-band designs. Experimental results are reported on several prototype filters. This solution augments the current state-of-the-art for narrow and moderate bandwidth adjustable filters.

articleTitle: Switched Piezoelectric SAW Resonator Using Vanadium Oxide
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE MTT-S International Microwave Filter Workshop (IMFW)
abstract: This paper presents implementation of a switched surface acoustic wave (SAW) piezoelectric resonator. The ON/OFF switching of acoustic resonance is achieved using vanadium oxide (VO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>) switches monolithically integrated with the piezoelectric resonator. High coupling coefficient and resonator Q values are achieved using multi-layered LiTaO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>/SiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>/Si stack. The resonator has a resonance frequency at 791 MHz with an electromechanical coupling coefficient of k<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">t</inf><sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>=10.2% and a Q of 400. Power handling performance of the proposed switched SAW resonator is also presented. The VO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> switch does not have any significant impact on the resonator Q and its power handling capability.

articleTitle: A Fault Tolerant Ka-band Power Amplifier Based on Corporate Combining for Radar Applications
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE MTT-S International Microwave Filter Workshop (IMFW)
abstract: A Ka-band solid state power amplifier for radar applications is presented. The amplifier uses sixteen low power modules combined by using a corporate network made with 90° hybrids. The proposed solution gives a good power combination and high robustness against auto oscillations. Moreover, the structure of the amplifier guarantees the so-called graceful degradation of the performance, meaning that if one or more amplifier module fails, the output power is only slightly affected. The amplifier has been fabricated and the experimental results validate the proposed design.

articleTitle: Shape Optimization of a Compact Dual-mode Filter Using Bézier Curves Parametrization
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE MTT-S International Microwave Filter Workshop (IMFW)
abstract: The shape of metallic components is optimized using a Bézier curves parametrization method for designing compact microwave filters with a numerical model. The parametrization method is applied to the boundaries of metallic posts placed in metallic cavities of a four-pole dual-mode filter, and it is coupled with a gradient-free method.
