Rounded metallic posts parametrized using Bézier curves are used for replacing classical cylindrical ones, knowing they can decrease microwave insertion loss. The initial dimensions of the structure are set by using cylindrical posts and the Bézier curves parameterization technique is applied for replacing cylindrical posts by rounded posts using a small set of variables.

articleTitle: Filter synthesis as a Structured Inverse Generalized Eigenvalue Problem
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE MTT-S International Microwave Filter Workshop (IMFW)
abstract: This letter intends to show that synthesis of a commensurate line filter can be treated as a Structured Inverse Generalized Eigenvalue Problem and so experience from the study of this general mathematical problem could be applied. The method in principle allows to optimize circuits of different topologies thus allowing to search for one that would suit the requirements the best.

articleTitle: The Recent Development of TE011 Mode Resonator Filters and Multiplexers
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE MTT-S International Microwave Filter Workshop (IMFW)
abstract: The TE011 mode resonator appears advantageous for presenting a higher quality factor (Qu) for the same volume, making it adequate for waveguide filters and multiplexers in terms of space applications. Yet difficulties emerge concerning spurious modes and negative couplings realization methods. This research explores approaches for fulfilling more advanced filter functions and realizing higher performance multiplexers using TE011 mode resonators. The synthesis approach and the electromagnetic (EM) design procedure are discussed.

articleTitle: Filtering Performance of Microacoustic-based Matching Networks for Wake-Up Applications
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE MTT-S International Microwave Filter Workshop (IMFW)
abstract: This paper explores different Matching Networks (MN) architectures based on acoustic microelectromechanical (MEMS) resonators for ultra-low-power Wake Up Receivers (WuRx) and compares them with established bulk element systems. The architectures are modeled and then compared in terms of passive voltage amplification (G<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">v</inf>), Fractional Bandwidth (BW<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</inf>), and Out-of-band Rejection (OBR) in the GSM-bands frequency range (800 MHz). According to this analysis, full MEMS-based and hybrid MEMS-based architectures outperform traditional MNs based on discrete elements, providing for sensibly larger G<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">v</inf>, OBR, and narrower BW<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</inf>. These results suggest that microacoustic resonators are suitable candidates to replace off-chip inductors in the MNs of next generation Internet of Things (IoT) wireless nodes.

articleTitle: Tunable resonator using a piston-like plunger
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE MTT-S International Microwave Filter Workshop (IMFW)
abstract: A new type of continuously tunable resonator is presented in this paper. This resonator is based on a parallelepipedal cavity in which a piston-shaped plunger is inserted. The TE<inf>101</inf> resonant mode can therefore be tuned as a function of the depth of this plunger. A first proof of concept is proposed in this paper and has been experimentally validated using metal and polymer additive manufacturing. This resonator is composed of a single 3D printed body and a separated plunger. The best tuning range achieved is between 11.12 and 14.58 GHz (27%) while the best quality factor goes up to 930 using copper plated 3D printed plunger.

articleTitle: Some Observations on the Coupling Matrix
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE MTT-S International Microwave Filter Workshop (IMFW)
abstract: Because the coupling matrix is a narrow band, lumped element approximation, its predicted performance does not always match what we realize in measured hardware. For many filter topologies, like the cavity combline, a network theory model or EM simulation is a more reliable predictor of actual performance.

articleTitle: Synthesis and Design of a Compact Electrically-Coupled Combline Filter with Multi-Sections Resonator
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE MTT-S International Microwave Filter Workshop (IMFW)
abstract: In this paper, a novel filter topology called Electrically-Coupled Combline (ECC) is proposed. The main asset of this topology compared to the standard Magnetic Coupling Combline (MCC) filter is that it is fully achievable with a planar technology. The synthesis of the filter is introduced and a practical implementation on a third-order filter is presented. To increase the electrical couplings to levels needed by this topology to achieved the desired relative passband (40%), the proposed Electrically Coupled Combline filter uses a Multi-Section line. Finally, the measurements are shown, and they appear to be consistent with the simulated results, exhibiting high compactness and good electrical performances. A third-order filter working at 125 MHz with a relative passband of 40% is finally presented to demonstrate the interest of this novel topology.

articleTitle: Coupling-Routing-Diagram Model of Non-Reciprocal Bandpass Filter With Single-Band-Forward and Dual-Band-Backward Behavior
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE MTT-S International Microwave Filter Workshop (IMFW)
abstract: An original approach to design non-reciprocal RF bandpass filters (BPFs) with spectrally-imbricated single- and dual-passband filtering transfer functions for the forward- and backward-signal-propagation directions, respectively, is reported. It exploits a two-path resonating stage, in which an isolator is inserted at one of its electrical paths in the backward direction to achieve this type of frequency-selective non-reciprocity. The operational foundations of the proposed non-reciprocal single-band-forward/dual-band-backward BPF in terms of coupling-routing diagram, which is generalized to model the isolator node, are provided. In addition, theoretical examples of the extension of this concept to higher-order filtering topologies by using multi-stage in-series-cascade schemes and to BPF designs with increased number of passbands for each transmission direction are shown.

articleTitle: Miniaturized Triple-Mode Bandpass Filter using Dielectric Resonators
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE MTT-S International Microwave Filter Workshop (IMFW)
abstract: This paper presents a compact triple-mode dielectric resonator bandpass filter based on a single waveguide cavity. Two barium titanate pucks are used in the design, placed in the middle of the metallic cavity to reduce the size of the filter. A third-order simplified Chebyshev bandpass filter is selected to verify the technique and simulated using HFSS software. The input and output coaxial probes are used to excite the degenerate EH11 modes, while the TM01 mode is excited using a vertical hole etched in the top of the barium titanate pucks. The resonator offers a size reduction ratio of about 15.6% compared with equivalent air-filled coaxial filters. The filter has finite transmission zeros on the high or low side of the passband.

articleTitle: Passive Networks for C-Band Multi-Carrier Wireless Backhaul Systems
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE MTT-S International Microwave Filter Workshop (IMFW)
abstract: This paper presents an overview of the passive components involved in multi-carrier single-antenna wireless backhauling systems, dedicated to enhancing data throughput for 5G deployment across the C-band. Three passive devices are the core building blocks for the presented configurations, all sharing the metallic hollow waveguide technology. The description and the design-to-manufacturing workflow is reported for a balanced coupler, a circulator, and an orthomode transducer. The required specifications together with measured data are reported for all the aforementioned devices.

articleTitle: High-Power X-band Diplexer for Quad-Band X/Ka Antenna Feed Chain System
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE MTT-S International Microwave Filter Workshop (IMFW)
abstract: This paper proposes a high-power X-band diplexer with low insertion loss and very high attenuation between channels for a new quad-band X/Ka antenna feed chain system developed by Anteral. The diplexer is composed of an E-plane T-junction which branches out a very compact TM<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">110</inf> band-pass filter, and a band-pass filter based on stubs. A prototype of the diplexer has been fabricated and measured, obtaining very good agreement between measurement and simulation. The proposed diplexer achieves more than 95 dB isolation between bands maintaining an insertion loss below 0.65 dB for both channels. Furthermore, the high-power handling has been estimated obtaining a power threshold of around 9.5 kW for ground systems.

articleTitle: Exploiting Input Phase in Extracted Pole Filters With a Single Nature for All Non-Resonant Nodes
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE MTT-S International Microwave Filter Workshop (IMFW)
abstract: This work presents how reflection phase can be exploited to design fully-canonical inline extracted pole filters featuring transmission zeros in both stopbands while implementing all non-resonant nodes of the same reactive nature. This approach allows to place up to two transmission zeros in the opposite stopband and overcomes the traditional concept that extracted pole sections should have non-resonant nodes of different nature depending on the stopband where they locate their pole. This feature is specially useful in technologies where only one nature of non-resonant nodes is easily fabricated. To validate the proposal two prototypes have been fabricated with only capacitive or only inductive non-resonant nodes.

articleTitle: Coupling-Matrix Filter Synthesis With Arbitrary Frequency-Variant Reactive Couplings
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE MTT-S International Microwave Filter Workshop (IMFW)
abstract: A generalized coupling-matrix-based filter-synthesis framework that allows to consider arbitrary frequency-variation profiles for reactive couplings is reported. The proposed formulation is based on the definition of the synthesis procedure as an inverse nonlinear eigenvalue problem (INEVP) so that the coupling matrix is build up from three different sets of eigenvalues. To this aim, an optimization-based procedure that exploits an iterative nonlinear least-squares solver with very-fast convergence features is adopted. For illustration purposes, a synthesis example that consists of a fourth-order bandpass filter in lumped-element and transmission-line realizations, where all couplings are frequency variant to generate five transmission zeros (TZs), is provided.

articleTitle: Design of Coupled-Resonator Filtering Network With Asymmetric Arbitrary Group-Delay Response and Frequency-Variant Coupling
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE MTT-S International Microwave Filter Workshop (IMFW)
abstract: A class of RF-analog-signal-processing passive circuits with bandpass filtering behavior and arbitrary prescribed group-delay characteristics is reported. The proposed approach is based on a cross-coupled-resonator network with frequency-dependent coupling to realize both symmetrical and asymmetrical frequency-variation patterns for the phase response. The synthesis procedure exploits a gradient-based optimization technique of the characteristic polynomials and a dispersive-coupling-matrix formulation to achieve the prescribed group-delay function. For illustration purposes, a third-order cross-coupled-resonator filter example in a triplet scheme with one dispersive coupling and linear-type group-delay frequency-variation profile is synthesized. A 2-GHz microstrip prototype of this example is also developed and tested to experimentally verify the devised design principle.

articleTitle: A Novel Realization of Fully Canonical and Pseudo-elliptic Wideband Waveguide Filters
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE MTT-S International Microwave Filter Workshop (IMFW)
abstract: This paper presents a novel realization of fully canonical and pseudo-elliptic wideband rectangular waveguide filters. Authors proposed a novel coupling structure in [1] that has the capability to realize a positive coupling, a negative coupling, or a TEM resonator by adjusting its length. A number of filters were realized using the novel coupling structure. In this paper, design of one fully canonical filter and four pseudoelliptic filters at the center frequency of 10 GHz is presented utilizing the novel coupling structure. One of the filter has an equiripple bandwidth of 1.5 GHz. Rigorous full-wave EM simulations have been performed, results demonstrate that the realization of such filters is feasible and desired number of transmission zeros can be generated at the prescribed positions.

articleTitle: Laser-machined ceramic band-pass filters development for mm-Wave applications
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE MTT-S International Microwave Filter Workshop (IMFW)
abstract: An overview of the laser-machined substrate technology (LMST) development, together with the difficulties and strategies adopted to achieve good electromagnetic (EM) performances in ceramic-based millimeter-wave (mm-Wave) devices are discussed. Several generations of band-pass filters were implemented at 40 GHz during the technology enhancement showing good characteristics without tuning corrections. The manufactured samples of each topology were characterized to assess the process repeatability, a necessary information for industrial massive millimeter-wave (mm-Wave) components fabrication.

articleTitle: Tunable Diplexer based on A Compact Hybrid-Coupled Filter Module (HCFM)
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE MTT-S International Microwave Filter Workshop (IMFW)
abstract: This paper presents a simple method for implementing tunable diplexer. The tunable diplexer is formed by cascading a bandpass filter with a compact hybrid-coupled filter module (HCFM), thereby simplifying the tuning complexity of diplexers. Particularly, the bandwidths and center frequencies of the diplexer can be modified by simply tuning the center frequencies of the bandpass filters and/or the HCFM. Tunability of the diplexer is investigated considering different scenarios. Moreover, the concept is validated through measurement results of two cascaded designs. Only the center frequencies of the bandpass filters in the cascaded systems are different. As expected, the resulting two diplexers have different center frequencies and bandwidths for each channel. Measurements results agree well with EM simulations for both designs.

articleTitle: mm-wave Dual-Mode Grounded Microstrip Patch BandPass Filter on 55-nm BiCMOS
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE MTT-S International Microwave Filter Workshop (IMFW)
abstract: This paper presents an original mm-wave dual-mode grounded microstrip patch bandpass filter operating at 200 GHz and implemented on 55-nm BiCMOS technology. Two filters were designed and simulated on different metallic layers. The unloaded quality factor reaches 22 and 29, depending on the Back-End-Of-Line flexible height. The achieved insertion loss is 2.5 dB and 1.8 dB, respectively. Both filters present a return loss better than 20 dB and fractional bandwidth around 20%. The introduced generated via-mode allowed the reduction of patch length to λ/5 with a total area size for both filters of 0.04 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>.

articleTitle: Design Advanced Microwave Filters with Redundancy
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE MTT-S International Microwave Filter Workshop (IMFW)
abstract: The conventional generalized Chebyshev filter functions and coupling matrix method have dominated microwave community and provided a "panacea" for microwave filter designs. However, forcing all filters to a paradigm virtually imposes redundant limitations and prevents achieving the optimal solutions under physical constraints. This paper breaks down the "mental barrier" in conventional approaches and exploits these redundancies to synthesize and design more advanced microwave filters. Three applications including redundant resonators, redundancies in filter polynomials and redundant resonant modes are elucidated as examples.

articleTitle: Filter Architecture Operating Beyond the Q Limit and With Real-Time Bandwidth Tunability
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE MTT-S International Microwave Filter Workshop (IMFW)
abstract: Novel radio paradigms such as software-defined radios and 5G pose stringent challenges for RF filter designers, as compact footprint, narrow-band operation, and real-time reconfigurability are required simultaneously. To address some of these challenges, we introduce a novel filter architecture based on spatio-temporal commutation of identical resonators that surpasses the limits dictated by resonator quality factor in narrow-band applications. This novel topology achieves outstanding real-time bandwidth control by tuning the commutation strategy. With a working point significantly different than conventional N-path networks, modulation frequencies which are a small fraction of the filter center frequency are demonstrated, relaxing electronics requirements. A compact PCB demonstration of such a filter operating at 100MHz is designed and measured, validating the simulated performance, with an insertion loss of 3dB and fractional bandwidths ranging from 50% to 100%, switching between four identical LC tanks.

articleTitle: Explicit formulas of the SM of a symmetrical combiner in terms of the ones of the elementary slices
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE MTT-S International Microwave Filter Workshop (IMFW)
abstract: Radial power combiners, that merge the power of N inputs in a single point, can provide low-losses and large-bandwidth solutions for high power and high performance devices. In this work, we provide a general formulation of the scattering parameters of power combiners having rotational symmetry, based on Floquet analysis and on proper use of the symmetry properties. Such analysis leads to a rigorous procedure that could be helpful to simplify both numerical simulation and design.

articleTitle: Wide Spurious-Free Waveguide Assembly For Military SATCOM Applications
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE MTT-S International Microwave Filter Workshop (IMFW)
abstract: This workshop paper presents the design and realization of a waveguide assembly comprising a bandpass filter and a H-plane bend. In contrast with standard design methods involving quasi-low pass corrugated or waffle-iron filters, the proposed assembly can provide a wide spurious free stopband by adopting specific design modifications/details in the realization of the bandpass filter and the bend. Capacitive irises, input/output reduced length cavities, as well as input/output notch elements, are the main design details embedded in the proposed bandpass filter. The passband of the assembly covers the downlink side of the military satellite communications Ka-band at 20.2 to 21.2 GHz, while the 60 dB stopband extends up to 46 GHz. The experimental results of a manufactured prototype conclude this article.

articleTitle: Ku-band differential lossy filter manufactured in thin-film on alumina technology
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE MTT-S International Microwave Filter Workshop (IMFW)
abstract: This paper presents the design and the fabrication of a compact and robust Ku-band differential bandpass filter, manufactured in thin-film on alumina. The 3-port device includes a balancing network which converts a single-ended input into a differential output. The goal is to achieve a flat in-band Insertion loss, keeping constrained the device size. An 8<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">th</sup> order lossy filter with 2 transmission zeros is synthetized using resistive cross-couplings to increase the IL flatness at the expenses of the absolute insertion loss. The balanced to unbalanced conversion is performed by a microstrip Lange coupler and a wideband Schiffman phase shifter. The device exhibits 0.7dB IL flatness in the operative bandwidth 12.75GHz-14.8GHz (FBW 14.5%) and an overall footprint of 14x26mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>. The device demonstrates also high robustness to thermal variations in the temperature range between -10 and 70°C.

articleTitle: Transversal Filters based on Stacked Crystal Filters with Spurious Mode Suppression
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE MTT-S International Microwave Filter Workshop (IMFW)
abstract: The transversal filter topology consists of resonators which require both positive and negative coupling to the input/output which typically necessitates the use of a BALUN. In this paper, transversal filters based on stacked crystal filters (SCFs) are presented. By inverting the polarity in one side of the SCF structure, both positive and negative couplings can be achieved, and the BALUN is no longer needed. In addition, a new approach to suppress spurious modes of SCFs is introduced.

articleTitle: Theoretical Design of Transmission-Line Reflectionless Bandstop Filter
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE MTT-S International Microwave Filter Workshop (IMFW)
abstract: This paper presents a straightforward design method of a reflectionless bandstop filter. As the conventional normalized lumped-element lowpass design parameters can be used in a filter design, it can be readily carried out without experiencing complicated math calculations. In addition, a transformation from a lumped-element structure to a distributed-element allows us to design a distributed-element reflectionless bandstop filter. For demonstration, a second-order reflectionless Butterworth bandstop filter of microstrip structure has been designed, fabricated, and measured.

articleTitle: An SIW-Fed Wideband Filtenna for 5G Millimeter-Wave Communications
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE MTT-S International Microwave Filter Workshop (IMFW)
abstract: This paper reports a substrate-integrated-waveguide (SIW)-fed wideband filtenna working in 5G millimeter-wave frequency. The proposed filtenna is developed by using three pieces of substrates and two pieces of bonding films. It comprises four main parts: an SIW feeding structure, a coupling slot, two L-shaped probes, and two slotted radiating patches. The use of L-shaped probes generates the filtering response in the lower stopband. At the same time, the slots etched on the radiating patches contribute to the acquirement of filtering response in the upper stopband. By carefully design the SIW feeding structure, the suppression level in the stopband can be significantly improved. The proposed filtenna has been simulated to show an impedance bandwidth of 25.1% (23.3-30 GHz) and a suppression level of greater than 18 dB. The proposed antenna is a good candidate in the 5G millimeter-wave communications system.

articleTitle: A Novel 2-Pole Tunable Coplanar Filter using Integrated Phase Change Material Switches
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE MTT-S International Microwave Filter Workshop (IMFW)
abstract: A novel tunable filter based on the use of PCM switches is presented. The filter center frequency can be switched between 5.95 and 6.8 GHz, using bi-stable Phase Change Material (PCM) RF switches. The 1 GHz bandpass filter has insertion loss between 4.5 and 5.5 dB. By integrating the bias circuit in the filter resonator, the loss attributed to the bias circuit can be minimized. Its influence on the filter response is discussed using various bias configurations.

articleTitle: Equal Ripple Filter Optimization
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE MTT-S International Microwave Filter Workshop (IMFW)
abstract: The general purpose optimizers found in most circuit analysis programs do not take advantage of the well defined transfer function of an equal ripple microwave filter. A dedicated optimization engine that uses this knowledge can be quite robust and efficient. We demonstrate several examples of how such a dedicated optimization engine can be used in practical microwave filter design.
